key_insight: PC-GNO learns the full mid-plane six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration by coupling graph neural operator updates with physics-informed interface impedance and spectral normalization.
engineering_relevance: It enables field-level surrogate prediction for penetration-resistant concrete design, linking mesoscale aggregate heterogeneity to actionable stress and energy-response maps.
method: Train on aggregate-resolved FEM penetration simulations in function space
Use impedance contrast across material interfaces to set message-passing strength
Constrain updates with spectral normalization to stabilize field evolution
evidence_signal: Trained on 359 validated FEM cases at 100, 135, and 165 m/s for concrete strengths of 14, 23, and 48 MPa, PC-GNO reached 80.16% mean accuracy and outperformed both a strong Fourier neural operator baseline and linear regression.
watch_item: Applicability is limited to the velocity, strength, and geometry regimes represented in the training/evaluation data, so extrapolation beyond those conditions should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
